node.name: catalog_credentials
node.signature: fn catalog_credentials( cli: &ServerCli, platform: Option<&PlatformTopology>, ) -> Result<Option<CatalogCredentials>, ServerConfigError>
node.doc:
Reads the catalog credentials from the topology's

`[auth.clients.flightdeck_catalog]` and the parsed CLI.



With a topology resolved, the table is the source of the client id, the

audience and the token endpoint. Outside `local` it is the only one: the

`--catalog-*` flags and their `FLIGHTDECK_CATALOG_*` variables are

checked aliases, and one that differs stops startup (RFD-j1jabh49,

decision 4). In `local` they override it, and with no topology they are

the interface. The secret is the table's `client_secret` reference when

it states one, and inline only in `local`, both read through the secret

resolver ([`catalog_client_secret`]).



A half-configured credential is a misconfiguration, not a request to

go anonymous. The catalog server refuses anonymous `ListEntries`, so

falling back would turn a typo into a permanently empty catalog and a

warning every refresh interval, which reads like a server fault.

node.name: a_view_over_a_replaced_view_reads_and_is_authorized_as_it_was_created
node.doc:
`DataFusion` binds a view when it is created: `CREATE VIEW v2 AS … FROM v1`

stores v1's definition of that moment, inlined, not a reference to v1.

Replacing v1 afterwards leaves v2 reading the old definition, and the

reader is authorized on the tables that old definition reads, so a

frozen definition over a restricted table is still refused.

node.doc:
Applies the read plan with the query's output lineage: an output whose

source columns are known takes the strongest mask among them (none when

none of them is masked, or when it reads no column at all); an output

whose lineage is unknown takes the plan's mask for its name, which ends

in the conservative fallback.

column's type, and an internal status when Arrow rejects the batch.

node.signature: async fn do_get( &self, request: Request<Ticket>, ) -> Result<Response<Self::DoGetStream>, Status>
node.doc:
Routes tickets: OQL streaming tickets go to `do_get_oql`, metadata

command tickets go to the appropriate metadata handler, everything else

is forwarded to the inner `QueryService`.

node.name: a_view_over_a_class_lends_the_analyst_none_of_its_tables
node.doc:
Views a content writer creates in pure-flight's semantic session lend an

analyst nothing: each is read through the tables beneath it, and the

class views beneath those, for the analyst's own use.

node.name: execute_oql
node.signature: async fn execute_oql( client: &mut FlightServiceClient<Channel>, oql: &str, ) -> Vec<arrow::array::RecordBatch>
node.doc:
Execute an OQL query via the two-step Flight protocol and collect all batches.



Step 1 — `do_action("oql.execute")` returns a ticket.

Step 2 — `do_get(ticket)` streams `FlightData` which is decoded to `RecordBatch`.

node.name: metadata_commands_require_authenticated_typestate
node.doc:
The Flight SQL metadata commands disclose which tables exist, so they

need the proof like every other handler. As in flightdeck, where

`information_schema` answers any authenticated caller, the listing is not

filtered per table.

node.doc:
Runs `oql` through `oql.execute` and its ticket; the plan is authorized

when the ticket is redeemed.
